plan.title: Renew what is due
plan.summary: Reads root card B, extends acme/B, renews acme-ca and acme-release, and builds the next trust files. It runs on your workstation, with a touch for every signature: 7 signatures, 7 touches.

steps.title: Check the plan
steps.detail: ritueel compares the plan with the bundle and with the history, and asks you to type the first eight characters of the digest: 7f3a9c1e.

steps.title: Read root card B
steps.detail: Reads every slot of root card B and compares it with the built-in layout. Nothing is written to the card. The yearly ceremony stays with one card: acme/B is the root of the year.

steps.title: Extend acme/B
steps.detail: A new X.509 root certificate over the same key and a new OpenPGP self-signature, so the root stays valid about three years from today. This is two more planned, recorded signatures of every card ceremony: the OpenPGP self-signature and the X.509 root certificate.
steps.whatChanges: acme/B stays valid for about three years from today

steps.title: Renew acme-ca
steps.detail: Certifies the key of the requester acme-gateway again under acme/B, for 13 months from the day of the ceremony. The old certificate stays valid until it ends.

steps.title: Renew acme-release
steps.detail: Binds the release subkey again under the OpenPGP primary of acme/B, for 13 months. The subkey is read with the admin role named in the configuration.
steps.whatChanges: A new binding for the release subkey

steps.title: Build the trust files
steps.detail: Builds the root list, the CA bundle, the CRLs, the SSH CA key list and the public OpenPGP keyring as trust sequence 8. The root of the year, acme/B, signs the root list, the SSH CA key list and its own CRL: three signatures. The CRL of acme/A is copied unchanged beside them.

steps.title: Write the record
steps.detail: Writes the record of this ceremony, which names the one before it and says it ran on the workstation, and its transcript.
steps.whatChanges: One new record in the history
